accuracy.reason: Source-supported distinctions are preserved across DNS/HTTP, recursive/referral roles, alias target dependence, ordinary TTL versus serve-stale, negative versus failed answers, steering and DNSSEC. Diagrams correctly distinguish cached old data from authoritative edits.

evidence.quote: SERVFAIL means resolution could not be completed, for example because the resolver could not obtain usable answers. It is not proof that the name does not exist. Resolution failures may also be cached to avoid repeatedly hammering failing DNS servers.

mechanisms.reason: Every card objective has actor/state/cause explanation: resolver steps, target lookup, old-TTL arithmetic, cached absence, health-policy changes, cached-client behavior and signature-chain purpose. Learner transfers time arithmetic and diagnoses distinct failure stages.

evidence.quote: A resolver caches the old address at 10:00 with a 300-second TTL. At 10:01 we change the address and lower TTL to 30 seconds. Its existing entry can still be ordinarily usable until 10:05; the edit does not rewrite that entry.

coherence.reason: The api.notes.example request anchors all cards. The hierarchy is explicitly illustrative, and slide 4 explicitly switches from alias to direct address before its TTL example. Terms are defined before their later dependencies.

evidence.quote: Now consider a direct address record for api.notes.example instead of the alias. TTL, or time to live, limits ordinary cache reuse in seconds. Each cache ages the TTL it received; it is not a worldwide update timer.

decisions.reason: Planning lower TTL early with overlap and monitoring, accepting query costs, requiring replacement capacity, separating diagnosis stages and preserving HTTPS checks provide practical choices and limits rather than instant-failover assurances.

evidence.quote: West must be reachable, healthy and have enough spare capacity for redirected work. A health signal is a sample, not a promise that every request succeeds; DNS changes do not create capacity or guarantee instant recovery.

clarity.reason: Names, record types, cache, actors, delegation and security terms receive first-use explanations. Worked times and two diagrams clarify responsibility and independent state without unnecessary protocol detail.

evidence.quote: The stub resolver is the client's local lookup helper. It asks a recursive resolver to obtain an answer on its behalf. An authoritative server answers from the records it serves for a zone, a managed portion of DNS names.

sourceChecks.claim: Cloudflare DNS explanation supports name-to-address discovery followed by separate web access; DNS data is not application health evidence.
AWS Route 53 resolution walkthrough follows recursive resolver, root, top-level and authoritative referrals and cached answers. The packet explicitly marks .example as a teaching hierarchy.
AWS record-type documentation defines A/AAAA address families and CNAME target name; RFC 1034 describes following aliases to answer the requested type.

RFC 8767 explicitly permits serve-stale beyond expiry during refresh failure; RFC 1034 TTL rules support reducing TTL before planned edits. Existing cache lifetime is not rewritten by a new authoritative TTL.

RFC 9520 distinguishes absence responses from resolution failure and requires failure caching; its RFC 2308 reference gives separate negative-answer TTL. Newly added positive TTL does not invalidate prior negative data.
AWS failover configuration requires health checks plus answer-selection policy. Cached DNS results and existing connection lifetimes explain why this cannot guarantee HTTP split or instant migration.

RFC 1034 distinguishes resolvers, authorities, cached data and delegation. Those dependencies explain fresh-lookup failure despite cached clients; a later HTTP error is a separate service-stage result.

RFC 4033 defines signature-chain origin/integrity validation and explicitly excludes confidentiality and access control. Its protection applies to DNS data and cannot replace HTTPS endpoint identity/encryption or prove application health.
